stops.note: a basket or box; in Dionysian mystery rites the sacred objects were carried in a covered kístē
a box; the bronze Ficoroni Cista, a 4th-century BC toiletry box found at Praeneste, is a famous example
borrowed from Latin for a box or coffer; the Franks Casket, an 8th-century whalebone chest, is carved with runic Old English verses
extended to the rib cage as the 'box' of the heart and lungs, replacing 'breast' in many uses; the 'chest of drawers' dates from the 1600s
stops.meaning: box; upper front of the body

current_meaning: the front of the body between neck and stomach; a large strong box
